in the announcement blog post for the 0.1.0 release, I want to do a "community showcase" section that just gives people an idea of what people are building with Roc!

I think more variety is better, to emphasize the whole "Roc is designed to be used in a long tail of domains" so if there's anything you've been working on that you'd be ok with my mentioning in the blog post, please feel free to share it here!

it would help to give a quick description of what the project is, where people can find it, and any related links, e.g. docs or blog posts.

feel free to share more than one - I likely won't have room in the post to include everything, but the more the better in terms of options as long as you're ok with sharing it! :smiley:
apps, packages, platforms, learning materials, etc. - anything is fair game
doesn't have to be open-source (we'll take your word for it if you say it's using Roc :smile: )
oh also it would be nice to mention lines of code, too - you can get that count easily by running roc loc

I've written the Safari Ride app in Roc. It's an animated screensaver that puts you in the seat of a motorcycle rider driving through about 20 road segments lined with trees, radio towers, and countless critters. UPL.

It's buried in a repo that has a bunch of smaller toy Roc apps: https://github.com/showell/roc-apps/tree/master/canvas_apps/safari

You can see it with other Roc apps here: https://roc.lynrummy.com/ (I also wrote a card game in Roc, a BASIC intrepreter in Roc, etc.)

Direct link to Safari Ride: https://roc.lynrummy.com/safari/

It's about 14k lines of code along with 6k lines of tests. It's all agent-written (Claude).

I describe the Safari Ride in my little Roc book: see #contributing > a little Roc book for some context, or just go straight to the book: https://roc.lynrummy.com/tutorial/introduction.html

The book excerpts about 2k out of the 14k lines of code.

The book is built partly using my roc-markdown library, which is here: https://github.com/showell/roc-markdown (also UPL, also agent written)

The markdown library is about 6k lines of Roc. The book uses another ~1400 lines of Roc for miscellaneous parts of its build process.

It's worth pointing out that most of my Roc apps are actually hybrids with other languages. So, for example, the Safari ride has a thin JS layer that sits along the Roc wasm. The book is partly built in Roc and partly build in Shale.

The BASIC interpreter runs as a playground here: https://roc.lynrummy.com/basic/basic.html

Code is here: https://github.com/showell/roc-apps/tree/master/basic (again, UPL and agent-written)

It's 6,733 lines of Roc in 12 files. The biggest Roc piece is https://github.com/showell/roc-apps/blob/master/basic/roc/Machine.roc at 2457 lines. Most of my Roc modules are much tinier!

I can write up more later ... but in case your not tracking we've got the roc-awesome repo which I've been trying to keep updated with everything that people talk about in Zulip and keep things that are relatively maintained.

https://github.com/lukewilliamboswell/roc-awesome
I know, but I'd like to get authors' permission here just to make sure people are ok with having their project(s) in the post :smile:
I give you permission to talk about roc-awesome :wink:
Feel free to mention Exercism and Roclet if you want.

Main things for me are:

Kai: a CLI tool for making environments & machines deterministic and reproducible, built as a friendly frontend for Nix with plugin support. The website is also built in roc-signals.

https://kai.blu.cx/
https://github.com/thebrandonlucas/kai

I'm also building an Ancient Greek digital library and toolkit I've been porting to Roc:

Study tool for learning Ancient Greek through spaced repetition:
https://study.lyceum.quest/
https://github.com/lyceum-quest/study

And this tool uses LLMs to generate glosses and prose translations for any work:

@Luke Boswell https://roc.lynrummy.com/ also tries to promote the versatility of roc-ray at the bottom of the page. Let me know if I can keep these on the page. I took a little liberty, given the license, of tweaking your examples. If you say "cut them" I will simply cut them. I can also tweak anything that you feel needs clarification or emphasis.

To be slightly more precise, the bottom half of the page promotes the versatility of Roc itself. It shows that an author can target a native platform with no intentions of publishing on the web, and then a second author can use the code nearly verbatim to move to a different platform and paradigm (web canvas).

Roxum is a web server platform that leverages Roc's strengths to make web development explicit, concise, and easy to reason about, with minimal boilerplate. Typed handlers, tags, and staged middleware are all designed around this philosophy.
https://github.com/KouYuume/roxum

If you'd like, mention Bliss Writer as well

https://blisswriter.app

Bliss is screenwriting software -- a word processor with special rules for screenplays. It is a TUI with the following parts:

  • Rust for terminal communication and other I/O using crossterm, ratatui and other crates
  • Rust for CRDT, using Loro
  • Roc code for screenplay layout and pagination
  • Roc app core (MVU)

Roc's colored purity is great. It allows to draw clear boundaries with less self discipline than any other language I tried.

The performance is very useful here, with every keystroke doing layout and pagination for subsequent pages. Currently my machine types at around 150-200fps for a long script, with scrolling at around 800fps. (These numbers exclude the terminal itself, it's just app performance). You can try yourself by clicking CTRL+SHIFT+ALT+0 in Bliss to show an FPS monitor.

https://github.com/zhenweigc/birbGBA
Inspired by FameBoy(GB emulator written in F#), so I decided to make a GBA emulator in Roc.
Still very WIP, as there is no sound, and the emulator throws explicit Err and force quit upon lots of UB documented in ARM7 ISA and Nintendo official manual.
However, after some arch optimization and 4 months of work, it does passes most of test ROMs from GBA-Tests, and can run some basic GBA games at full speed(until it got hit by an opcode with UB)

This project relies heavily on Luke's Roc-Ray to render graphics, will probably rely on it to support sound.


To run it, just build it(against window.roc, runner is headless and is used for early testing), put a BIOS(you can use Emi Huang's emibios/nintendo official BIOS, should all work) and a gamerom under the same folder. Name them to be bios.bin & game.gba

yeah right the frontend UI is just crappy and baremetal, as I do not have much experience in that, and I am a bit lazy :P will add some basic UIs for rom & bios selections later.

And I did use mature project such as NanoBoyAdvance & mGBA as references. Oh, and LLMs are used to Nudge me when I got lost. And during optimiation it helps me to find what drags the game slow.

Richard Feldman said:

I think more variety is better, to emphasize the whole "Roc is designed to be used in a long tail of domains" so if there's anything you've been working on that you'd be ok with my mentioning in the blog post, please feel free to share it here!

You can use any of my projects. Some ideas

Packages (just pure Roc)

  • plume :: type safe API for making interactive charts using Plotly.js
  • roc-docx :: parse and generate .docx files compatible with Word, LibreOffice, Google Docs
  • roc-font :: read OpenType and TrueType fonts and shape text into positioned glyphs
  • roc-graph-layout :: graph layout algorithms (similar to ELK etc) and a Mermaid diagram parser and render
  • roc-parser :: Parser combinators, plus CSV|OFX|QIF|YAML|XML|HTML|SVG|MathML|JSON|MD|ASCIIDOC|HTTP|Roc
  • roc-pdf :: Generate PDF 2.0 PDF/A-4 documents
  • roc-time :: Dates and times
  • weaver :: CLI argument parser similar to Rust clap

Platforms

  • starter templates for Zig/Rust/Go
  • basic-sgg :: static site generation for Roc (support's markdown and asciidoc formats)
  • roc-fuzz :: fuzzing and property based testing based on libFuzzer with builtin performance observatory
  • roc-ray :: Games and graphics based on raylib
  • roc-gui :: Experimental platform for building GUI apps based on GPUI
  • roc-signals :: Signals based UI framework for the Web
  • embed-roc-in-dotnet :: embed Roc in a .NET application

Tooling

  • roc-blueprint :: development environments and workflows on top of Nix
  • roc-automation :: opinionated approach for managing Roc packages and platforms, shared actions and a book

roc-regex is a regular expression matching engine. It's generally competitive performance-wise with other state of the art implementations, including Rust's regex crate on machines with 128-bit wide SIMD.

roc-markdown is a CommonMark + GFM compliant markdown parser.

trantor is an extensible platform system that's designed to build a set of Rust crates into a single platform which was developed in support of...

Kite, which is a native GUI platform and my main effort in Roc. It's from scratch from the shaders up with Clay as a starting point (immediate mode) and for LoC it's around 170k Rust and 50k Roc not including whitespace and comment lines. It's my take on web programming without the browser so the programming model is basically Elm and the styling is basically Tailwind. A majority of the browser's styling capabilities are implemented (gradients, shadows, text decorations, borders, images, grid and flexbox). Most of the demos are flat because it's easy and that's the current trend but the platform has the full set of capabiliites:

There's an animation system with support for element entry/exit transitions, forward/reverse animation chaining, closed-form spring animation, and auto-filmstrip repeated animations so the full app render doesn't happen on every cursor blink. There's a widget system including a data grid and rich text editing.






Since it's built on web concepts, I have an alternate roc platform for running on the DOM that translates the platform calls to the web equivalent instead of the native stack. I've only done simpler demos on it as a proof of concept but it drops the wasm bundle from 9MB (full app in WASM rendering in a WebGL context) to ~300k (DOM nodes+CSS) for the counter demo.

Finally, I have it built for android and running on my e-ink tablet. Many of the resource consumption and styling decisions were made to facilitate apps running well on the device. It doesn't screenshot that well but a non-JVM app with custom e-ink waveform support allows 30ms interaction latency in the PDF reader app instead of the hundreds the vendor app takes.

I'll add that I'm pretty desperate for work so if anybody is looking to hire or contract, I'd be grateful.
